page: Amazon Web Services r8a.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a single dedicated x86_64 physical core and 1 vCPU powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 4 MB L3 cache, complemented by support for advanced vector instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI.

The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio characteristic of the r8a memory-optimized profile. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, instead relying on network-attached storage solutions. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-threaded performance balanced against strict single-core resource limits. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests (3753.98), single-threaded gzip compression (41.09 GB/sec), and Geekbench single-core execution (2790.0). However, overall multi-core metrics, including multi-core Geekbench (2787.0) and PassMark CPU scores (3479.37), land in the lower quartiles due to the presence of only a single dedicated thread.

Uncached memory throughput is stable, yielding 46.87 GB/sec for 256 MB reads and 34.48 GB/sec for writes. The instance offers strong single-threaded CPU capability paired with an 8 GB memory pool in a low-resource footprint, making it suitable for lightweight in-memory caching nodes, development database replicas, single-threaded batch processing, and lightweight web serving services.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.medium is a memory-optimized instance featuring 1 dedicated vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz and 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 without local storage or GPU hardware. The CPU architecture supports AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, leading to top-tier single-core computational results in Geekbench (2790.0) and gzip compression. Multi-core throughput remains restricted by the single-core configuration. With a 1 Gbps baseline network profile and stable uncached memory throughput, the r8a.medium provides an entry-level memory-heavy environment suitable for small in-memory caches, small database instances, microservices, and single-threaded batch jobs.
